basic_1.title: Which command shows text on the screen?
basic_1.prompt: In Python, what is the magic command we use to show a message on the screen?
basic_1.explanation: The print() command is like a megaphone for the computer! Whatever you put inside the parentheses will appear on the screen. For example: print("Olá!") shows "Olá!" on the screen.

basic_2.title: Text needs quotes
basic_2.prompt: To write text in Python, we need to put it between quotes. For example: "Olá mundo"
basic_2.explanation: That's right! Text in Python goes between quotes ("double quotes" or 'single quotes'). That way Python knows it's text and not a command!

basic_3.title: Complete the code to say "Olá"
basic_3.prompt: Complete the code below to show "Olá, mundo!" on the screen:
basic_3.explanation: We use print() to show things on the screen! It's the first command every programmer learns. Now you know how to write messages for the whole world to see! 🌍

basic_4.title: What appears on the screen?
basic_4.prompt:
If we run this code, what will appear?

print(5 + 3)
basic_4.explanation: Python is very smart! When we ask it to calculate 5 + 3, it does the math and shows the result: 8! Python can be your personal calculator! 🧮

basic_5.title: Comments are executed
basic_5.prompt: Lines that start with # are comments and are NOT executed by Python.
basic_5.explanation: Lines with # are little notes for you or other programmers, but Python ignores them! It's like writing a note in your notebook that only you will read. 📝

turtle_1.title: Drawing a Square
turtle_1.prompt: Let's draw a square! Use the commands forward(100) and right(90) to make the 4 lines.
turtle_1.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners of 90 degrees. By moving and turning 4 times, we close the square! ⏹️

basic_parsons_1.title: Print Order
basic_parsons_1.prompt: Put the blocks in order to show "Olá" and then "Mundo".
basic_parsons_1.explanation: Python reads code from top to bottom! First "Olá", then "Mundo".

basic_6.title: Single or Double Quotes?
basic_6.prompt: Which of these options is correct for creating text in Python?
basic_6.explanation: In Python, you can use either single quotes (' ') or double quotes (" ")! What matters is opening and closing with the same kind. 😉

basic_7.title: What is # for?
basic_7.prompt: When we put a # at the beginning of a line, Python:
basic_7.explanation: The # creates a comment! Python skips that line, so you can write notes to yourself without breaking the code! 📝

basic_hard_1.title: Several Prints
basic_hard_1.prompt: Complete it to show your name, age and city on 3 separate lines:
basic_hard_1.explanation: Each print() shows one line! To show 3 different pieces of information, we use 3 prints, one for each thing. 📋

basic_hard_2.title: Calculator with Print
basic_hard_2.prompt: Build the code to calculate 10 + 5 * 2 and show the result:
basic_hard_2.explanation: First we store the calculation in a variable, then we use print to show it! Remember: multiplication comes before addition! 🧮

basic_8.title: Mixing Quotes
basic_8.prompt: Can I use single quotes INSIDE double quotes?
basic_8.explanation: Yes! If you started with double quotes, you can use single quotes inside the text (and vice versa). Example: print("O gato fez 'miau'") 😺

basic_9.title: Comment on the Same Line
basic_9.prompt: Can I put a comment on the same line as code? Ex: print("Oi") # Isso é um oi
basic_9.explanation: Yes! Python reads the code until it finds the #. Everything AFTER the # is ignored. That way you can explain the code right there! 📝

basic_10.title: Joining with a Comma
basic_10.prompt: What happens if we use a comma in print? Ex: print("Oi", "Mundo")
basic_10.explanation: The comma in print separates things and adds a space automatically! It's super useful for joining text and numbers. 🤝
options: Prints with a space between them

basic_11.title: Uppercase or Lowercase?
basic_11.prompt: Does the command `Print("Olá")` (with a capital P) work?
basic_11.explanation: Python is "case sensitive"! `print` must always be all lowercase. `Print` or `PRINT` don't work! 🚫

basic_12.title: Quotes inside Quotes
basic_12.prompt: Which of these options works without an error?
basic_12.explanation: Both work! The secret is mixing: if you use double quotes outside, use single quotes inside (and vice versa). That way Python doesn't get confused! 🎭

basic_13.title: Invisible Code
basic_13.prompt: Which of these lines will Python completely IGNORE?
basic_13.explanation: Python ignores everything that starts with #! For Python, that line doesn't exist. It's perfect for leaving notes! 👻

basic_14.title: Magic Quotes
basic_14.prompt: Which command is WRONG because of the quotes?
basic_14.explanation: Quotes must match at the beginning and the end! If you started with double quotes, end with double quotes. No mixing! 🎭

basic_15.title: Ignoring Code
basic_15.prompt: Complete the code so that Python ignores the line (a comment):
basic_15.explanation: The # symbol makes Python ignore everything after it on the same line. That's how we write comments! 🤫

basic_16.title: Blank Line
basic_16.prompt: How do we skip a line (show an empty line) using print?
basic_16.explanation: If you use `print()` with nothing inside, it shows an empty line! It's great for separating text and organizing what appears on the screen. 📄

boss_battle_1.explanation: The Portal Guardian protects the exit. He only lets through those who speak his language (Python)!
